title: Cap. 1 vocabulary: Reprobatio — Scripture voice vs school sense
pass_a_gloss: Concerning the opposite vocabulary of Reprobation we will now say a few things. As to the voice, in the sacred Scriptures reprobus and reprobare are referred rather to the present condition of impious human beings than to the eternal ordination of God concerning them. For ἀδόκιμος or reprobate is called one who lives impiously, and does not bear himself as a son of God, but by deeds shows himself to be rejectitious, spurious, and adulterine: And God is said to repel, reject, or reprobate such ones because of their impurity, just as goldsmiths reject adulterine coins. Moreover in Augustine (who treated this matter more richly and more clearly than the other Fathers) the vocabularies of the reprobate and of reprobating, in that sense in which they are now frequented in the School of the Theologians, occur either rarely or not at all. But nevertheless it must be known that the thing itself is openly contained in the sacred Scriptures. First, when those things are affirmed in the sacred Scriptures whence by clear and necessary consequence the reprobation of certain ones is deduced: As when certain marked persons are said to be elect and predestined by God before the foundations of the world were laid. For the election of some imports the passing-by or rejection of others. Second, when by equivalent words the decree of reprobation is expressed: as when God is said never to have known certain ones, not to have given them to Christ, to be unwilling to have mercy on certain ones, not to have written certain ones' names in the book of life, and other things of that kind, which liquidly prove that there was in the Divine mind and will a discrimination of elect and non-elect from eternity. Finally, although Augustine and the other Fathers do not much use this vocabulary of reprobation, nevertheless they use others which are equally valid. For those whom the School calls reprobates, they call foreknown and predestined unto destruction.
pass_b_english: On the opposite word, Reprobation, a few points. As for the bare term, Scripture's "reprobate" and "to reprobate" point more to the present state of the ungodly than to God's eternal decree about them. ἀδόκιμος — a reprobate — is one who lives ungodly, does not carry himself as a son of God, and by his deeds shows himself counterfeit, spurious, adulterate. God is said to reject or reprobate such people because of that impurity, as goldsmiths throw out counterfeit coins. Even in Augustine — who treated this matter more richly and clearly than the other Fathers — "reprobate" and "reprobating" in the school sense barely appear, or do not appear at all. Still, the thing itself is plainly in Scripture. First, when Scripture affirms what forces the reprobation of some by clear necessary consequence: as when certain named persons are said elect and predestined by God before the world's foundations were laid. Election of some imports passing by — rejecting — others. Second, when equivalent phrases express the decree: God is said never to have known some, not to have given them to Christ, to refuse mercy to some, not to have written some names in the book of life — and the like, which plainly prove that from eternity the Divine mind and will marked a difference between elect and non-elect. Finally, though Augustine and the other Fathers seldom use the school word "reprobation," they use other words that mean the same. Those the School calls reprobates, they call foreknown and predestined to destruction.
source_text: De opposito Reprobationis vocabulo jam paucis dicemus. Ad vocem quod attinet, in sacris Scripturis reprobus & reprobare referuntur potius ad praesentem hominum impiorum conditionem, quam ad aeternam Dei de illis ordinationem. Nam ἀδόκιμος sive reprobus appellatur qui impie vivit, nec gerit se pro filio Dei, sed factis ostendit se esse rejectitium, spurium & adulterinum: Atque Deus tales repellere, rejicere sive reprobare dicitur propter illorum impuritatem, sicut aurifices rejiciunt nummos adulterinos. Quinetiam apud Augustinum (qui hanc materiam uberius & dilucidius quam caeteri Patres tractavit) reproborum & reprobandi vocabula, eo sensu quo nunc in Schola Theologorum frequentantur, aut raro, aut non omnino occurrunt. Sed tamen sciendum est rem ipsam in sacris Scripturis aperte contineri. Primo, quando ea affirmantur in sacris Scripturis unde clara & necessaria consecutione deducitur quorundam reprobatio: Ut cum certae quaedam & signatae personae dicuntur electi & praedestinati a Deo ante jacta mundi fundamenta. Electio enim aliquorum praeteritionem sive rejectionem aliorum infert. Secundo, quando verbis aequivalentibus reprobationis decretum exprimitur: ut cum Deus dicitur quosdam nunquam nosse, non dedisse Christo, nolle quorundam misereri, non scripsisse quorundam nomina in libro vitae, & id genus alia, quae liquido probant, apud Divinam mentem & voluntatem fuisse discrimen electorum & non-electorum ab aeterno. Postremo, licet Augustinus, aliique Patres non multum utantur hoc vocabulo reprobationis, tamen aliis utuntur quae perinde valent. Nam quos Schola appellat reprobatos, illi vocant praescitos & praedestinatos ad interitum.
